title.raw: 卷412 列傳一百九十九 左宗棠

sentences.zh: 列傳一百九十九

translations.literal: Biographies 199
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 199

sentences.zh: 左宗棠

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang

sentences.zh: 左宗棠，字季高，湖南湘陰人。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang, styled Jigao, was a man of Xiangyin in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang, whose courtesy name was Jigao, came from Xiangyin in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父觀瀾，廩生，有學行。

translations.literal: His father Guanlan was a licentiate and possessed learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guanlan held licentiate standing and was a man of learning and integrity.

sentences.zh: 宗棠，道光十二年舉人，三試禮部不第，遂絕意仕進，究心輿地、兵法。

translations.literal: Zongtang became a provincial graduate in the twelfth year of Daoguang; three times he took the metropolitan examination at the Ministry of Rites without passing, and thereafter abandoned all thought of official advancement, devoting himself to geography and military science.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang passed the provincial examination in 1832, but after failing the metropolitan examination three times he gave up any hope of an official career and threw himself into geography and military strategy.

sentences.zh: 喜為壯語驚眾，名在公卿間。

translations.literal: He delighted in bold words that startled the crowd, and his name circulated among the high ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He loved grand pronouncements that astonished listeners, and his reputation spread among the court elite.

sentences.zh: 嘗以諸葛亮自比，人目其狂也。

translations.literal: He once compared himself to Zhuge Liang, and people regarded him as mad.
translations.idiomatic: He once likened himself to Zhuge Liang, and many considered him unhinged.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼亟稱之，謂橫覽九州，更無才出其右者。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi repeatedly praised him, saying that surveying the Nine Provinces horizontally, there was no talent superior to his.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi spoke of him again and again, declaring that across the realm there was no one to match his ability.

sentences.zh: 年且四十，顧謂所親曰：「非夢卜夐求，殆無幸矣！」

translations.literal: When he was nearly forty, he turned and said to those close to him: "Unless sought through dream-divination and distant inquiry, there is probably no hope!"
translations.idiomatic: By the time he was nearly forty, he told his intimates, "Unless heaven seeks one out through oracle and omen, there is little hope of fortune!"

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，廣西盜起，張亮基巡撫湖南，禮闢不就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng, bandits rose in Guangxi; Zhang Liangji became governor of Hunan and ceremonially invited him, but he would not come.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign, rebellion broke out in Guangxi. When Zhang Liangji took office as Hunan governor, he invited Zongtang with full ceremony, but Zongtang declined.

sentences.zh: 林翼敦勸之，乃出。

translations.literal: Lin Yi earnestly urged him, and then he came forth.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Linyi pressed him repeatedly did he agree to emerge.

sentences.zh: 敘守長沙功，由知縣擢同知直隸州。

translations.literal: Recording his merit in defending Changsha, he was promoted from magistrate to sub-prefect of Zhili Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in the defense of Changsha he was promoted from county magistrate to sub-prefect of Zhili Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 亮基移撫山東，宗棠歸隱梓木洞。

translations.literal: Liangji was transferred to govern Shandong, and Zongtang returned to seclusion at Zimu Cave.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangji was transferred to Shandong, Zongtang withdrew again to seclusion at Zimu Cave.

sentences.zh: 駱秉章至湖南，復以計劫之出佐軍幕，倚之如左右手。

translations.literal: When Luo Bingzhang arrived in Hunan, he again by stratagem compelled him to come out and assist in the military secretariat, relying on him as on right and left hands.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Bingzhang came to Hunan, he again contrived to draw Zongtang out to serve on his military staff, relying on him as on his own two hands.

sentences.zh: 僚屬白事，輒問：「季高先生雲何？」

translations.literal: When subordinates reported affairs, he would always ask: "What does Master Jigao say?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his staff brought him business, he would ask, "What does Master Jigao say?"

sentences.zh: 由是忌者日眾，謗議四起，而名日聞。

translations.literal: From this, those who envied him daily grew numerous, slander and criticism arose on all sides, yet his fame daily spread.
translations.idiomatic: Envy of him mounted daily, slander spread on every side, and his reputation only grew.

sentences.zh: 同里郭嵩燾官編修，一日，文宗召問：「若識舉人左宗棠乎？

translations.literal: His fellow townsman Guo Songtao held the post of compiler; one day the Wenzong Emperor summoned and asked: "Do you know the provincial graduate Zuo Zongtang?
translations.idiomatic: His fellow townsman Guo Songtao served as a Hanlin compiler. One day the Xianfeng Emperor asked him, "Do you know the provincial graduate Zuo Zongtang?

sentences.zh: 何久不出也？

translations.literal: Why has he long not come forth?
translations.idiomatic: Why has he stayed out of service so long?

sentences.zh: 年幾何矣？

translations.literal: How many years old is he now?
translations.idiomatic: How old is he now?

sentences.zh: 過此精力已衰，汝可為書諭吾意，當及時出為吾辦賊。」

translations.literal: Past this his vigor will already have declined; you may write a letter conveying my intent, that he should timely come forth and handle the bandits for me."
translations.idiomatic: After that his strength will be spent. Write to him with my wishes and tell him to come out in good time and fight the rebels for me."

sentences.zh: 林翼聞而喜曰：「夢卜夐求時至矣！」

translations.literal: When Linyi heard this he rejoiced and said: "The time of dream-divination and distant inquiry has come!"
translations.idiomatic: When Linyi heard the news he exclaimed with delight, "The hour of oracle and omen has arrived at last!"

sentences.zh: 六年，曾國籓克武昌，奏陳宗棠濟師、濟餉功，詔以兵部郎中用，俄加四品卿銜。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Zeng Guofan captured Wuchang and memorialized Zongtang's merits in aiding the army and provisions; an edict appointed him for use as a director in the Ministry of War, and shortly thereafter he was given the fourth-rank honorary title of Court Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856, after Zeng Guofan took Wuchang, he memorialized Zongtang's contributions in supplying troops and funds. The court appointed Zongtang a director in the Ministry of War and soon added a fourth-rank honorary court title.

sentences.zh: 會秉章劾罷總兵樊燮，燮構於總督官文，為蜚語上聞，召宗棠對簿武昌，秉章疏爭之不得。

translations.literal: It happened that Bingzhang impeached and dismissed regional commander Fan Xie; Xie framed matters with Governor Guan Wen, and slander reached the throne; Zongtang was summoned to answer charges at Wuchang, and Bingzhang memorialized in protest without success.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Bingzhang had impeached and removed regional commander Fan Xie. Fan enlisted Governor Guan Wen to spread rumors to the court, and Zongtang was summoned to face charges at Wuchang. Bingzhang protested in a memorial but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 林翼、國籓皆言宗棠無罪，且薦其才可大用。

translations.literal: Linyi and Guofan both said Zongtang was innocent and moreover recommended that his talent could be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: Both Linyi and Guofan declared Zongtang innocent and urged that his talents deserved major employment.

sentences.zh: 詹事潘祖廕亦誦言總督惑於浮辭，故得不逮。

translations.literal: Junior Mentor Pan Zuyin also repeatedly stated that the governor was misled by empty words, and therefore he was not arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Mentor Pan Zuyin likewise argued that the governor had been swayed by idle talk, and so Zongtang was not taken into custody.

sentences.zh: 俄而朝旨下，命以四品京堂從國籓治軍。

translations.literal: Shortly an imperial order came down, commanding him as a fourth-rank capital official to follow Guofan in managing the army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an imperial order arrived appointing him a fourth-rank capital official to serve under Guofan in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，國籓創立湘軍，諸軍遵其營制，獨王珍不用。

translations.literal: At first Guofan founded the Xiang Army; all armies followed his camp regulations, but Wang Zhen alone did not use them.
translations.idiomatic: When Guofan first formed the Xiang Army, other forces adopted his camp organization, but Wang Zhen alone kept his own system.

sentences.zh: 宗棠募五千人，參用珍法，號曰「楚軍」。

translations.literal: Zongtang recruited five thousand men, partly employing Zhen's methods, and styled them the "Chu Army."
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang raised five thousand men, drawing partly on Zhen's methods, and called the force the Chu Army.

sentences.zh: 十年八月，宗棠既成軍而東，偽翼王石達​​開竄四川，詔移師討蜀。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the tenth year, after Zongtang had completed his army and marched east, the false Wing King Shi Dakai fled into Sichuan, and an edict ordered the army transferred to campaign in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In August 1860, after Zongtang had mustered his force and marched east, the rebel Wing King Shi Dakai fled into Sichuan and the court ordered the army shifted to attack there.

sentences.zh: 國籓、林翼以江、皖事急，合疏留之。

translations.literal: Guofan and Linyi, because affairs in Jiangsu and Anhui were urgent, jointly memorialized to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan and Linyi, finding the Jiangsu and Anhui fronts critical, submitted a joint memorial asking that he be kept on the scene.

sentences.zh: 時國籓進兵皖南，駐祁門，偽侍王李世賢、忠王李秀成糾眾數十萬圍祁門。

translations.literal: At that time Guofan advanced into southern Anhui and encamped at Qimen; the false Attendant King Li Shixian and Loyal King Li Xiucheng gathered several hundred thousand men and besieged Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan was then advancing into southern Anhui and had encamped at Qimen, where the rebel Attendant King Li Shixian and Loyal King Li Xiucheng massed several hundred thousand men to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 宗棠率楚軍道江西，轉戰而前，遂克德興、婺源。

translations.literal: Zongtang led the Chu Army by way of Jiangxi, fighting as he advanced, and then captured Dexing and Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang led the Chu Army through Jiangxi, fighting his way forward until he took Dexing and Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 賊趨浮梁景德鎮，斷祁門餉道。

translations.literal: The bandits moved toward Fuliang and Jingdezhen, cutting the supply route to Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pushed toward Fuliang and Jingdezhen and severed the supply line to Qimen.

sentences.zh: 宗棠還師擊之，大戰於樂平、鄱陽，殭屍十餘萬，世賢易服逃，而徽州賊亦遁浙江。

translations.literal: Zongtang turned his army to strike them; great battles were fought at Leping and Poyang, with corpses numbering more than a hundred thousand; Shixian changed clothes and fled, and the Huizhou bandits also escaped into Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang wheeled back to attack them. At Leping and Poyang he fought major battles that left more than a hundred thousand dead. Shixian disguised himself and fled, and the Huizhou rebels also withdrew into Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 自是江、皖軍勢始振。

translations.literal: From this the military situation in Jiangsu and Anhui first revived.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the armies in Jiangsu and Anhui began to recover their strength.

sentences.zh: 十一年，詔授太常寺卿，襄辦江南軍務，乃率楚軍八千人東援浙。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, an edict appointed him Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to assist in Jiangnan military affairs; he then led eight thousand men of the Chu Army east to aid Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to assist in Jiangnan military affairs and led eight thousand Chu Army troops east to relieve Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 朝命國籓節制浙江，國籓薦宗棠足任浙事。

translations.literal: The court ordered Guofan to supervise Zhejiang; Guofan recommended that Zongtang was fully adequate to handle Zhejiang affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court placed Zhejiang under Guofan's overall command, and Guofan recommended Zongtang as fully capable of managing Zhejiang affairs.

sentences.zh: 宗棠部將名者，劉典、王開來、王文瑞、王沐，數軍單薄，不足資戰守；

translations.literal: Among Zongtang's notable subordinate generals were Liu Dian, Wang Kailai, Wang Wenrui, and Wang Mu; several armies were thin and insufficient to support fighting and defense;
translations.idiomatic: His best-known subordinate commanders were Liu Dian, Wang Kailai, Wang Wenrui, and Wang Mu, but their forces were too few to sustain prolonged combat;

sentences.zh: 乃奏調蔣益澧於廣西，劉培元、魏喻義於湖南，皆未至，而宗棠以數千人策應七百餘裡，指揮若定，國籓服其整暇。

translations.literal: he therefore memorialized to transfer Jiang Yili from Guangxi and Liu Peiyuan and Wei Yuyi from Hunan; none had yet arrived, yet Zongtang with several thousand men coordinated operations over more than seven hundred li, directing affairs as if at ease; Guofan admired his composure under pressure.
translations.idiomatic: so he requested transfers of Jiang Yili from Guangxi and Liu Peiyuan and Wei Yuyi from Hunan. None had yet arrived, yet with only a few thousand men Zongtang coordinated operations across more than three hundred miles with unshaken command, and Guofan marveled at his calm mastery.

sentences.zh: 已而壕州陷，复疏薦之，遂授浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: Before long Haozhou fell; he again memorialized recommending him, and Zongtang was then appointed governor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Haozhou soon fell, he memorialized again on Zongtang's behalf, and Zongtang was appointed governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時浙地唯湖、衢二州未陷賊，國籓與宗棠計，以保徽州，固饒、廣為根本。

translations.literal: At that time in Zhejiang only the two prefectures of Hu and Qu had not fallen to bandits; Guofan and Zongtang planned to hold Huizhou and secure Rao and Guang as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time only the Hu and Qu prefectures in Zhejiang still held out. Guofan and Zongtang agreed to defend Huizhou and make Rao and Guang their strategic base.

sentences.zh: 奏以三府屬縣賦供其軍，設婺源、景德、河口三稅局裨之，三府防軍悉隸宗棠。

translations.literal: They memorialized that the tax levies of counties subordinate to the three prefectures should supply his army; three tax bureaus were established at Wuyuan, Jingde, and Hekou to supplement this, and all defensive troops of the three prefectures were placed under Zongtang.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized that the land tax of counties in the three prefectures should feed his army, established tax offices at Wuyuan, Jingde, and Hekou to supplement revenue, and placed all garrison troops of the three prefectures under Zongtang's command.

sentences.zh: 賊大舉犯婺源，親督軍敗之。

translations.literal: The bandits launched a major attack on Wuyuan; he personally directed the army and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels launched a major assault on Wuyuan, he personally directed the army and routed them.

sentences.zh: 同治元年正月，詔促自衢規浙。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Tongzhi, an edict urged him to advance from Qu toward Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1862 an edict pressed him to advance from Quzhou toward the heart of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 宗棠奏言：「行軍之法，必避長圍，防後路。

translations.literal: Zongtang memorialized, saying: "The method of marching armies must avoid prolonged encirclement and guard the rear route.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang replied in a memorial: "In campaigning one must avoid long encirclements and secure the line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 臣軍入衢，則徽、婺疏虞，又成糧盡援絕之勢。

translations.literal: If my army enters Qu, then Huizhou and Wuyuan will be left lightly guarded, and we will again fall into a situation of exhausted provisions and cut-off relief.
translations.idiomatic: If my army enters Quzhou, Huizhou and Wuyuan will be left exposed, and we shall again face starvation with no relief.

sentences.zh: 今由婺源攻開化，分軍扼華埠，收遂安，使饒、廣相庇以安，然後可以製賊而不為賊制。」

translations.literal: Now by attacking Kaihua from Wuyuan, dividing the army to hold Huabu, recovering Suian, and letting Rao and Guang shelter each other in safety, only then can we control the bandits and not be controlled by the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: I propose to strike Kaihua from Wuyuan, detach troops to hold Huabu, recover Suian, and let Rao and Guang shield one another. Only then can we master the rebels instead of being mastered by them."

sentences.zh: 二月，克遂安。

translations.literal: In the second month, Suian was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Suian was taken.

sentences.zh: 世賢自金華犯衢州，連擊敗之。

translations.literal: Shixian from Jinhua attacked Quzhou; Zongtang repeatedly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian advanced from Jinhua against Quzhou, but Zongtang defeated him again and again.

sentences.zh: 而皖南賊复陷寧國，遣文瑞往援，克績溪。

translations.literal: Meanwhile southern Anhui bandits again captured Ningguo; he dispatched Wenrui to aid, and Jixi was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels in southern Anhui meanwhile retook Ningguo. He sent Wenrui to relieve the position and recovered Jixi.

sentences.zh: 十一月，喻義克嚴州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yuyi captured Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yuyi took Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，益澧及高連升、熊建益、王德榜、餘佩玉等克金華、紹興，浙東諸郡縣皆定。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Yili together with Gao Liansheng, Xiong Jianyi, Wang Debang, Yu Peiyu, and others captured Jinhua and Shaoxing; all prefectures and counties of eastern Zhejiang were settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1863, Yili together with Gao Liansheng, Xiong Jianyi, Wang Debang, Yu Peiyu, and others took Jinhua and Shaoxing, and all of eastern Zhejiang was secured.

sentences.zh: 杭州賊震怖，悉眾拒富陽。

translations.literal: The Hangzhou bandits were shaken with terror and gathered all their forces to resist at Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels at Hangzhou were thrown into panic and massed their entire force at Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 時諸軍爭議乘勝取杭城，宗棠不喜攻堅，謂皖南賊勢猶盛，治寇以殄滅為期，勿貪近功。

translations.literal: At that time the various armies disputed taking advantage of victory to seize Hangzhou city; Zongtang disliked assaulting strongholds, saying southern Anhui bandit strength was still great, that suppressing bandits should aim at complete extermination, and one must not covet immediate success.
translations.idiomatic: Other commanders urged an immediate assault on Hangzhou, but Zongtang disliked storming walled cities. He argued that rebel strength in southern Anhui remained formidable, that suppression must aim at total annihilation, and that one must not chase quick gains.

sentences.zh: 乃自金華進軍嚴州，令劉典將八千人會文瑞防徽州，以培元、德榜駐淳安、開化，而益澧攻富陽。

translations.literal: He then advanced from Jinhua to Yanzhou, ordered Liu Dian to lead eight thousand men to join Wenrui in defending Huizhou, stationed Peiyuan and Debang at Chunan and Kaihua, and had Yili attack Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: He marched from Jinhua to Yanzhou, ordered Liu Dian with eight thousand men to join Wenrui in defending Huizhou, posted Peiyuan and Debang at Chunan and Kaihua, and set Yili against Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 劾罷道府及失守將吏十七人，舉浙士吳觀禮等賑荒招墾，足裕軍食。

translations.literal: He impeached and dismissed seventeen circuit-intendants, prefects, and officers who had lost their posts; he recommended Zhejiang scholars such as Wu Guanli to relieve famine and recruit cultivation, fully supplying army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed seventeen circuit officials, prefects, and commanders who had lost their posts, and appointed Zhejiang scholars such as Wu Guanli to relieve famine and promote resettlement until army provisions were ample.

sentences.zh: 四月，授浙閩總督，兼巡撫事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, he was appointed Governor-General of Zhejiang and Fujian, concurrently handling governor affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was appointed governor-general of Zhejiang and Fujian, retaining concurrent charge of the governorship.

sentences.zh: 劉典軍既至皖南，遂留屯。

translations.literal: After Liu Dian's army had reached southern Anhui, it remained encamped there.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Dian's force reached southern Anhui, it remained stationed there.

sentences.zh: 益澧攻富陽，軍僅萬餘人，皆病疫，宗棠亦患瘧困憊，富陽圍久不下，乃簡練舊浙軍，兼募外國軍助之攻。

translations.literal: Yili attacked Fuyang; the army had only a little more than ten thousand men, all stricken with epidemic disease; Zongtang also suffered malaria and was worn down; the siege of Fuyang long would not fall, and he then drilled the old Zhejiang army and also recruited foreign troops to assist in the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yili besieged Fuyang with barely ten thousand men, all stricken by epidemic disease. Zongtang himself was racked by malaria. When the siege dragged on, he retrained the old Zhejiang forces and hired foreign auxiliaries to help take the city.

sentences.zh: 七月，李鴻章江蘇軍入浙攻嘉善，嘉興寇北援，於是水陸大舉攻富陽，克之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Li Hongzhang's Jiangsu army entered Zhejiang to attack Jiashan; Jiaxing bandits came north in relief; thereupon land and water forces launched a major attack on Fuyang and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Li Hongzhang's Jiangsu army entered Zhejiang against Jiashan. Rebels from Jiaxing marched north to relieve the position, and then a combined land and river assault took Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 益澧等長驅搗杭州，魏喻義、康國器攻餘杭。

translations.literal: Yili and others drove straight to storm Hangzhou; Wei Yuyi and Kang Guoqi attacked Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yili and others pressed straight toward Hangzhou while Wei Yuyi and Kang Guoqi attacked Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 宗棠以杭賊恃餘杭為犄角，非先下餘杭，收海寧，不能斷嘉、湖援濟，躬至餘杭視師。

translations.literal: Zongtang, because Hangzhou bandits relied on Yuhang as a flank position, said that unless Yuhang was first taken and Haining recovered, Jia and Hu relief could not be cut off; he personally went to Yuhang to inspect the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang judged that the Hangzhou rebels depended on Yuhang as a flank and that Jiaxing and Huzhou could not be cut off until Yuhang and Haining were taken first. He went in person to Yuhang to direct operations.

sentences.zh: 是時皖賊古隆賢反正，官軍連下建平、高淳諸邑。

translations.literal: At this time the Anhui bandit Gu Longxian turned to the orthodox side; government troops in succession took Jianping, Gaochun, and other districts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Anhui rebel Gu Longxian defected to the government side, and imperial forces in succession recovered Jianping, Gaochun, and other districts.

sentences.zh: 金陵賊呼秀成入謀他竄，獨世賢踞溧陽，與廣德賊比，中梗官軍。

translations.literal: The Jinling bandits called Xiucheng in to plan another breakout; Shixian alone held Liyang, adjacent to Guangde bandits, blocking government troops in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanjing rebels summoned Xiucheng to plan another breakout. Shixian alone held Liyang alongside the Guangde rebels, blocking government forces in the center.

sentences.zh: 鴻章既克嘉善，上言當益軍攻嘉興。

translations.literal: After Hongzhang had captured Jiashan, he memorialized that troops should be increased to attack Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: After Hongzhang took Jiashan, he memorialized that reinforcements should be sent against Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 會浙師取常州，而廣德賊已由寧國竄浙。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhejiang troops took Changzhou, while Guangde bandits had already from Ningguo fled into Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Zhejiang forces took Changzhou, Guangde rebels had already broken from Ningguo into Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 宗棠慮賊分擾江西、福建，乃檄張運蘭率所部趨福建，召劉典防江西。

translations.literal: Zongtang feared the bandits would divide to harass Jiangxi and Fujian; he therefore ordered Zhang Yunlan to lead his command toward Fujian and summoned Liu Dian to defend Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the rebels might split off to harass Jiangxi and Fujian, Zongtang ordered Zhang Yunlan toward Fujian and recalled Liu Dian to guard Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 海寧賊蔡元隆以城降，更名元吉，後遂為驍將。

translations.literal: The Haining bandit Cai Yuanlong surrendered the city and changed his name to Yuanji; he later became a fierce general.
translations.idiomatic: The Haining rebel Cai Yuanlong surrendered the city, changed his name to Yuanji, and later became one of Zongtang's fiercest commanders.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，元吉會江蘇軍克嘉興。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, Yuanji joined the Jiangsu army and captured Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1864, Yuanji joined the Jiangsu army and took Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 杭州賊陳炳文勢蹙約降，猶慮計中變，乘雨急攻之，夜啟門遁，杭州复，餘杭賊汪海洋亦東走。

translations.literal: The Hangzhou bandit Chen Bingwen, his situation pressed, agreed to surrender, yet still feared a change in the plan; taking advantage of rain he pressed the attack urgently; at night they opened the gates and fled; Hangzhou was recovered, and the Yuhang bandit Wang Haiyang also fled east.
translations.idiomatic: The Hangzhou rebel Chen Bingwen, hard pressed, agreed to surrender but still feared a trap. Zongtang attacked in heavy rain. That night the rebels opened the gates and fled. Hangzhou was recovered, and the Yuhang rebel Wang Haiyang also fled east.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，加太子少保銜，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was given the honorary title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: On report of victory he received the honorary title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and was granted the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 移駐省城，申軍禁，招商開市，停杭關稅，減杭、嘉、湖稅三之一。

translations.literal: He moved his headquarters to the provincial capital, proclaimed military prohibitions, invited merchants and opened markets, suspended Hangzhou customs duties, and reduced Hangzhou, Jia, and Hu taxes by one third.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his headquarters to the provincial capital, enforced military discipline, invited merchants back, reopened markets, suspended Hangzhou customs duties, and cut taxes in Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou by one third.

sentences.zh: 益澧為布政使，亦輕財致士，一時翕然稱之。

translations.literal: Yili served as provincial treasurer and likewise was generous with wealth to win scholars; for a time all praised him together.
translations.idiomatic: Yili, serving as provincial treasurer, was likewise generous in winning men of talent, and for a time the two were praised together throughout the province.

sentences.zh: 群賊聚湖州，乃移軍合圍，先攻菱湖。

translations.literal: The mass of bandits gathered at Huzhou; he then moved the army to join in encirclement, first attacking Linghu.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining rebels massed at Huzhou. He shifted his army to complete the encirclement and struck first at Linghu.

sentences.zh: 三月，江蘇軍克常州，賊敗竄徽、婺，趨江西。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Jiangsu army captured Changzhou; defeated bandits fled through Huizhou and Wuyuan toward Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Jiangsu army took Changzhou. Defeated rebels fled through Huizhou and Wuyuan toward Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 世賢踞崇仁，海洋踞東鄉，宗棠以賊入江西為腹心患，奏請楊岳斌督江西、皖南軍，以劉典副，從之。

translations.literal: Shixian held Chongren and Haiyang held Dongxiang; Zongtang, because bandits entering Jiangxi was a vital threat, memorialized requesting Yang Yuebin to supervise Jiangxi and southern Anhui armies with Liu Dian as deputy; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian held Chongren and Haiyang held Dongxiang. Zongtang, seeing rebel penetration of Jiangxi as the gravest threat, memorialized for Yang Yuebin to command the Jiangxi and southern Anhui armies with Liu Dian as deputy, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 六月，曾國荃克江寧，洪秀全子福瑱奔湖州，俄复潰走，磔於南昌。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Zeng Guoquan captured Jiangning; Hong Xiuquan's son Fuzhen fled to Huzhou, but soon again broke and fled; he was dismembered at Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zeng Guoquan took Nanjing. Hong Xiuquan's son Fuzhen fled to Huzhou, broke again soon after, and was executed by dismemberment at Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 七月，克湖州，盡定浙地。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Huzhou was captured and all of Zhejiang was settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Huzhou fell and all of Zhejiang was pacified.

sentences.zh: 論功，封一等恪靖伯。

translations.literal: In reckoning merit, he was enfeoffed as a first-class Kejing Earl.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as first-class Earl Kejing.

sentences.zh: 餘賊散走徽、寧、江西、廣東，折入汀州，福建大震。

translations.literal: Remaining bandits scattered through Huizhou, Ning, Jiangxi, and Guangdong, turned into Tingzhou, and Fujian was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining rebels scattered through Huizhou, Ningguo, Jiangxi, and Guangdong, turned into Tingzhou, and all Fujian was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 乃奏請之總督任，以益澧護巡撫，增調德榜軍至閩。

translations.literal: He then memorialized requesting the governorship there, with Yili acting as governor, and increased transfer of Debang's army to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to take the Fujian governorship himself, left Yili as acting governor of Zhejiang, and brought Debang's army into Fujian as reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，江蘇軍郭松林來會師，賊棄漳州出大埔。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year, the Jiangsu army's Guo Songlin came to join forces; the bandits abandoned Zhangzhou and went out through Dabu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1865, Guo Songlin of the Jiangsu army joined the campaign. The rebels abandoned Zhangzhou and broke out through Dabu.

sentences.zh: 五月，進攻永定。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, he advanced to attack Yongding.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he advanced against Yongding.

sentences.zh: 世賢、海洋既屢敗，傷精銳過半，歸誠者三萬。

translations.literal: Shixian and Haiyang, having been repeatedly defeated, had lost more than half their elite troops; those who submitted numbered thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian and Haiyang, repeatedly defeated, had lost more than half their best troops, and thirty thousand men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 宗棠進屯漳州，躡賊武平。

translations.literal: Zongtang advanced and encamped at Zhangzhou, pursuing the bandits to Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang advanced to Zhangzhou and pursued the rebels to Wuping.

sentences.zh: 於是賊竄廣東之鎮平，而福建亦定。

translations.literal: Thereupon the bandits fled into Zhenping in Guangdong, and Fujian was also settled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then fled into Zhenping in Guangdong, and Fujian was pacified as well.

sentences.zh: 乃檄康國器、關鎮平兩軍入粵，王開琳一軍入贛防江西，劉典軍趨南安防湖南，留高連升、黃少春軍武平，伺賊進退。

translations.literal: He then ordered Kang Guoqi's and Guan Zhenping's two armies into Guangdong, Wang Kailin's army into Gan to defend Jiangxi, Liu Dian's army toward Nan'an to guard Hunan, leaving Gao Liansheng's and Huang Shaochun's armies at Wuping to watch the bandits' advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the armies of Kang Guoqi and Guan Zhenping into Guangdong, Wang Kailin's force into Jiangxi, and Liu Dian's toward Nan'an to guard Hunan, while Gao Liansheng and Huang Shaochun remained at Wuping to watch the rebels' movements.

sentences.zh: 六月，賊大舉犯武平，力戰卻之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, bandits launched a major attack on Wuping; after fierce fighting they were repelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the rebels launched a major assault on Wuping and were beaten back after hard fighting.

sentences.zh: 世賢投海洋，為所戕，賊黨益猜貳。

translations.literal: Shixian threw himself on Haiyang and was killed by him; the bandit faction grew ever more suspicious and divided.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian threw in his lot with Haiyang and was killed by him, and rebel morale grew ever more fractured.

sentences.zh: 詔以宗棠節制三省諸軍。

translations.literal: An edict placed all armies of the three provinces under Zongtang's supervision.
translations.idiomatic: An edict placed all armies of the three provinces under Zongtang's command.

sentences.zh: 十月，賊陷嘉應，宗棠移屯和平琯溪。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, bandits captured Jiaying; Zongtang moved his camp to Heping Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the rebels took Jiaying, and Zongtang shifted his headquarters to Heping Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 德榜慮帥屯孤懸，自請當中路。

translations.literal: Debang feared the commander's camp was isolated and exposed, and volunteered to hold the central route.
translations.idiomatic: Debang, fearing the commander's camp was dangerously exposed, volunteered to take the central route.

sentences.zh: 劉典聞德榜軍趨前，亦引軍疾進。

translations.literal: Liu Dian, hearing Debang's army was pressing forward, also led his army in rapid advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Dian heard Debang's army was pushing forward, he too advanced at speed.

sentences.zh: 猝遇賊，敗，賊追典，掠德榜屯而過，槍環擊之，輒反走。

translations.literal: Suddenly encountering bandits, he was defeated; the bandits pursued Dian, swept past Debang's camp, and when guns fired on them from all sides they at once turned and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They suddenly met the rebels and were defeated. The rebels pursued Liu Dian, swept past Debang's camp, and when fired on from every side at once turned and fled.

sentences.zh: 是夜降者逾四萬，言海洋中砲死矣，士氣愈奮。

translations.literal: That night those who surrendered exceeded forty thousand; they said Haiyang had been killed by cannon in the midst of battle, and morale grew ever more exalted.
translations.idiomatic: That night more than forty thousand surrendered, reporting that Haiyang had been killed by cannon fire. Government morale soared.

sentences.zh: 時鮑超軍亦至，賊出拒，又大敗之。

translations.literal: At that time Bao Chao's army also arrived; the bandits came out to resist and were again greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Chao's army also arrived. The rebels came out to resist and were routed again.

sentences.zh: 合閩、浙、江、粵軍圍嘉應。

translations.literal: Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, and Guangdong armies combined to besiege Jiaying.
translations.idiomatic: Forces from Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, and Guangdong combined to besiege Jiaying.

sentences.zh: 十二月，賊開城遁，扼諸屯不得走，跪乞免者六萬餘，俘斬賊將七百三十四，首級可計數者萬六千，詔賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the bandits opened the city and fled; blocked at the various camps and unable to escape, more than sixty thousand knelt begging mercy; seven hundred thirty-four bandit generals were captured and killed; countable heads numbered sixteen thousand; an edict granted double-eyed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the rebels opened the gates and fled but were blocked at the encampments. More than sixty thousand knelt begging mercy. Seven hundred thirty-four rebel commanders were captured or killed and sixteen thousand heads were counted. An edict granted him double-eyed peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，凱旋。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, he returned in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1866 he returned in triumph.

sentences.zh: 宗棠以粵寇既平，首議減兵並餉，加給練兵。

translations.literal: Zongtang, because Guangdong bandits were already pacified, was first to propose reducing troops and combining pay, and increasing allotments for drilled soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: With the Guangdong rebels pacified, Zongtang was the first to propose cutting troop numbers and consolidating pay while increasing funds for drilled militia.

sentences.zh: 又以海禁開，非製備船械不能圖自強，乃創船廠馬尾山下，薦起沈葆楨主其事。

translations.literal: He also held that with the maritime prohibition lifted, without preparing ships and weapons self-strengthening could not be planned; he therefore founded a shipyard below Mawei Mountain and recommended Shen Baozhen to direct the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that with maritime trade reopened, China could not pursue self-strengthening without building ships and arms, so he founded a shipyard at Mawei and recommended Shen Baozhen to run it.

sentences.zh: 會王師征西陲回亂久無功，詔宗棠移督陝、甘。

translations.literal: It happened that the imperial army's campaign against the western frontier Muslim rebellion had long been without success; an edict transferred Zongtang to govern Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the court's campaign against the Muslim rebellion on the western frontier had long stalled, and Zongtang was ordered to take over Shaanxi and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 十月，簡所部三千人西發，令劉典別募三千人期會漢口，中途以西捻張總愚竄陝西，命先入秦勦賊。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he selected three thousand men from his command to march west, ordered Liu Dian separately to recruit three thousand men to rendezvous at Hankou; midway, because the western Nian leader Zhang Zongyu had fled into Shaanxi, he was ordered first to enter Qin to suppress bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he led three thousand of his own troops west and ordered Liu Dian to raise another three thousand to meet at Hankou. En route, when the western Nian leader Zhang Zongyu broke into Shaanxi, he was told to enter Qin first and suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 陝、甘回眾數至百萬，與捻合。

translations.literal: Muslim communities in Shaanxi and Gansu numbered up to a million, and joined with the Nian.
translations.idiomatic: Muslim rebels in Shaanxi and Gansu numbered as many as a million and had joined forces with the Nian.

sentences.zh: 宗棠行次武昌，上奏曰：「臣維東南戰事利在舟，西北戰事利在馬。

translations.literal: When Zongtang reached Wuchang on his march, he memorialized, saying: "Your servant considers that in southeastern warfare the advantage lies in boats, while in northwestern warfare the advantage lies in horses.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuchang on his march west he memorialized: "In the southeast, victory depends on boats; in the northwest, on horses.

sentences.zh: 捻、回馬隊馳騁平原，官軍以步隊當之，必無幸矣。

translations.literal: Nian and Muslim cavalry gallop across the plains; if government troops meet them with infantry, there can be no hope of success.
translations.idiomatic: Nian and Muslim horsemen sweep the plains. If government troops meet them on foot, they cannot hope to prevail.

sentences.zh: 以馬力言，西產不若北產之健。

translations.literal: Speaking of horse strength, western breeds are not as robust as northern breeds.
translations.idiomatic: In horse power, western breeds are weaker than northern ones.

sentences.zh: 捻馬多北產，故捻之戰悍於回。

translations.literal: Nian horses are mostly northern breeds; therefore Nian fighting is fiercer than Muslim fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Nian horses are mostly from the north, which is why the Nian fight more fiercely than the Muslims.

sentences.zh: 臣軍止六千，今擬購口北良馬習練馬隊，兼制雙輪砲車。

translations.literal: Your servant's army has only six thousand; now I propose to purchase fine horses from Koubei and drill cavalry, while also making double-wheeled gun carriages.
translations.idiomatic: My force has only six thousand men. I propose to buy fine horses from the northern frontier, train cavalry, and build double-wheeled gun carriages.

sentences.zh: 由襄、鄧出紫荊關，徑商州以赴陝西。

translations.literal: From Xiang and Deng through Zijing Pass, straight by Shangzhou to reach Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: I shall march from Xiangyang and Dengzhou through Zijing Pass and Shangzhou into Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 經營屯田，為久遠之規。

translations.literal: I shall organize military colonies as a plan for the long term.
translations.idiomatic: I shall establish military colonies as a long-term plan.

sentences.zh: 是故進兵陝西，必先清關外之賊；

translations.literal: Therefore in advancing into Shaanxi, one must first clear bandits outside the passes;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore to advance into Shaanxi one must first clear the rebels beyond the passes;

sentences.zh: 進兵甘肅，必先清陝西之賊；

translations.literal: in advancing into Gansu, one must first clear Shaanxi's bandits;
translations.idiomatic: to advance into Gansu one must first clear Shaanxi;

sentences.zh: 駐兵蘭州，必先清各路之賊：然後餽運常通，師行無阻。

translations.literal: in stationing troops at Lanzhou, one must first clear bandits on all routes: only then will supply transport flow steadily and the army march without obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: and to station troops at Lanzhou one must first clear every route: only then will supplies move steadily and the army march without hindrance.

sentences.zh: 至於進止久速，隨機赴勢，伏乞假臣便宜，寬其歲月，俾得從容規畫，以要其成。」

translations.literal: As for advance and halt, duration and speed, adapting to circumstances and following the momentum, I humbly beg that Your Majesty grant me discretionary authority, allow ample time, and enable me to plan at leisure so as to secure final success."
translations.idiomatic: As for when to advance or halt and how fast to move, I beg Your Majesty to grant me discretion and ample time so that I may plan at leisure and bring the campaign to success."

sentences.zh: 六年春，提兵萬二千以西。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, he led twelve thousand troops west.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1867 he led twelve thousand troops west.

sentences.zh: 議以砲車制賊馬，而以馬隊當步賊。

translations.literal: It was proposed to use gun carriages to control rebel horses, and use cavalry to meet infantry bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was to use gun carriages to break the rebel cavalry and horse troops to meet the rebel infantry.

sentences.zh: 捻倏見砲車，皆不戰狂奔。

translations.literal: When the Nian suddenly saw gun carriages, all fled without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Nian caught sight of the gun carriages they fled without fighting.

sentences.zh: 時陝西巡撫劉蓉已解任，總督楊岳斌請歸益急。

translations.literal: At that time Shaanxi Governor Liu Rong had already been relieved, and Governor-General Yang Yuebin's request to return grew ever more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi governor Liu Rong had already left office, and Governor-General Yang Yuebin was pressing ever harder to go home.

sentences.zh: 詔寧夏將軍穆圖善署總督，宗棠以欽差大臣督軍務。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Ningxia General Mutu Shan acting governor-general; Zongtang as Imperial Commissioner supervised military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Mutu Shan, general of Ningxia, was appointed acting governor-general, while Zongtang served as Imperial Commissioner in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 分軍三道入關，而皖南鎮總兵劉松山率老湘軍九千人援陝，山西按察使陳湜主河防，其軍皆屬焉。

translations.literal: The army was divided into three columns to enter the passes; meanwhile Southern Anhui garrison commander Liu Songshan led nine thousand veterans of the old Xiang Army to aid Shaanxi, and Shanxi judicial commissioner Chen Ni directed river defense; all these armies were placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: He divided his force into three columns to enter the passes. Liu Songshan of the old Xiang Army brought nine thousand men to reinforce Shaanxi, and Shanxi judicial commissioner Chen Ni took charge of river defense. All came under Zongtang's command.

sentences.zh: 松山既屢敗捻，又合蜀軍將黃鼎、皖軍將郭寶昌，大破之富平。

translations.literal: Songshan, having repeatedly defeated the Nian, then joined Sichuan commander Huang Ding and Anhui commander Guo Baochang and inflicted a great defeat on them at Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: After repeatedly defeating the Nian, Songshan joined Huang Ding of the Sichuan army and Guo Baochang of the Anhui army and routed them at Fuping.

sentences.zh: 捻掠三原，沿渭北東趨，回則分黨西犯，麕集北山。

translations.literal: The Nian plundered Sanyuan and along the north of the Wei marched east; Muslims meanwhile split into factions and attacked west, gathering thickly in the northern hills.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian raided Sanyuan and marched east along the north bank of the Wei, while Muslim bands split westward and massed in the northern hills.

sentences.zh: 宗棠以捻強於回，當先制捻。

translations.literal: Zongtang held that the Nian were stronger than the Muslims and that the Nian should be controlled first.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang judged the Nian the stronger foe and resolved to deal with them first.

sentences.zh: 檄諸軍憑河結營，期蹙而殲之涇、洛間。

translations.literal: He ordered all armies to camp along the river, intending to compress and annihilate them between Jing and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his armies to camp along the river and crush the Nian between the Jing and Luo.

sentences.zh: 捻乘軍未集，又折而西渡涇、渭，窺豫、鄂。

translations.literal: The Nian, taking advantage before the armies had gathered, again turned west and crossed the Jing and Wei, watching Henan and Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Before the armies could concentrate, the Nian turned west again, crossed the Jing and Wei, and threatened Henan and Hubei.

sentences.zh: 已而大軍進逼，勢不復能南，乃趨白水。

translations.literal: Before long the great army pressed close; they could no longer move south and therefore hurried toward Baishui.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force closed in, they could no longer push south and fled toward Baishui.

sentences.zh: 乘大風雨，鋌走入北山。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of great wind and rain, they dashed into the northern hills.
translations.idiomatic: In a driving storm they bolted into the northern hills.

sentences.zh: 宗棠防捻、回合勢，且北山荒瘠，師行糧不繼，因急扼耀州。

translations.literal: Zongtang feared Nian and Muslim forces would combine, and moreover the northern hills were barren and poor so that army provisions could not follow; he therefore urgently seized Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a Nian-Muslim combination, and knowing the northern hills were too barren to feed an army, he urgently seized Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，捻敗走宜川，別黨果竄耀州，合回匪攻同官。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the Nian were defeated and fled toward Yichuan; a separate band indeed fled into Yaozhou and joined Muslim rebels to attack Tongguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the defeated Nian fled toward Yichuan while another band broke into Yaozhou and joined Muslim rebels against Tongguan.

sentences.zh: 留防軍不能禦，典、連升軍馳救，大破之。

translations.literal: The garrison left to defend could not resist; Dian's and Liansheng's armies rushed to relieve and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The local garrison could not hold. Liu Dian and Gao Liansheng rushed to the rescue and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 諸軍將雖屢敗捻，終牽於回，師行滯；

translations.literal: Although the various commanders repeatedly defeated the Nian, they were ultimately held back by the Muslims and the army's march was delayed;
translations.idiomatic: Although his commanders repeatedly beat the Nian, they were constantly drawn off by Muslim raids and the campaign stalled;

sentences.zh: 而捻大眾在宜川者益北擾延長，掠綏德，趨葭州，回亦自延安出陷綏德。

translations.literal: meanwhile the main Nian body at Yichuan increasingly harassed north into Yanchang, plundered Suide, and pressed toward Jiazhou; Muslims also from Yan'an came out and captured Suide.
translations.idiomatic: while the main Nian force at Yichuan raided north into Yanchang, plundered Suide, and pressed toward Jiazhou, and Muslims from Yan'an also took Suide.

sentences.zh: 宗棠自以延、綏迭失，上書請罪，部議革職。

translations.literal: Zongtang, holding himself responsible for the successive loss of Yanchang and Suide, submitted a letter requesting punishment; the ministry deliberated stripping him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang blamed himself for the loss of Yanchang and Suide, submitted a confession, and the ministry recommended his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 時北山及扶、岐、汧、隴、邠、鳳諸回，所在響應。

translations.literal: At that time Muslims of the northern hills and of Fu, Qi, Qian, Long, Bin, and Feng all responded everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Muslims throughout the northern hills and in Fu, Qi, Qian, Long, Bin, and Feng rose everywhere at once.

sentences.zh: 捻自南而北，千有餘裡，回自西而東，亦千有餘裡。

translations.literal: The Nian from south to north stretched more than a thousand li; the Muslims from west to east also more than a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian stretched more than five hundred miles from south to north, and the Muslims more than five hundred miles from west to east.

sentences.zh: 陝西主客軍能戰者不及五萬，然回當之輒敗。

translations.literal: Shaanxi's native and guest armies able to fight numbered less than fifty thousand, yet whenever they met Muslims they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Fewer than fifty thousand government troops in Shaanxi could actually fight, yet they were beaten whenever they met the Muslims.

sentences.zh: 松山等克綏德，回走米脂，捻復分道南竄。

translations.literal: Songshan and others captured Suide; Muslims fled to Mizhi; the Nian again split and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Songshan retook Suide. The Muslims fled to Mizhi while the Nian again split and fled south.

sentences.zh: 於是劉厚基出東北追回，松山等循西岸要捻。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liu Houji went out northeast to pursue and recover them; Songshan and others along the west bank intercepted the Nian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Houji pursued northeast while Songshan blocked them along the west bank.

sentences.zh: 師抵宜川，回大出遮官軍，留戰一日，破之；

translations.literal: When the army reached Yichuan, Muslims came out in force to block government troops; after fighting one day they were defeated;
translations.idiomatic: At Yichuan the Muslims massed to block the army; after a day of fighting they were broken;

sentences.zh: 而捻遂取間道逾山至壺口，乘冰橋渡河。

translations.literal: but the Nian then took a bypath over the mountains to Hukou and crossed the river on an ice bridge.
translations.idiomatic: but the Nian took a mountain path to Hukou and crossed the Yellow River on the ice.

sentences.zh: 宗棠奉朝旨，山右毗連畿輔，令自率五千人赴援，以劉典代督陝甘軍。

translations.literal: Zongtang received the court order that Shanxi adjoined the capital region; he was commanded personally to lead five thousand men to aid, with Liu Dian replacing him in supervising the Shaanxi-Gansu army.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered east because Shanxi bordered the capital region, Zongtang led five thousand men personally to the relief while Liu Dian took over the Shaanxi-Gansu command.

sentences.zh: 是年十二月，捻自垣曲入河南，益北趨定州，遊騎犯保定，京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year, the Nian from Yuanchu entered Henan, pressed ever north toward Dingzhou, roaming cavalry violated Baoding, and the capital was placed under alert.
translations.idiomatic: That December the Nian entered Henan from Yuanchu, pressed toward Dingzhou, raided Baoding, and the capital went on alert.

sentences.zh: 詔切責督兵大臣，自宗棠、鴻章及河南巡撫李鶴年、直隸總督官文，皆奪職。

translations.literal: An edict sharply rebuked the ministers supervising troops; from Zongtang and Hongzhang to Henan Governor Li Henian and Zhili Governor Guan Wen, all were stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: The court sharply rebuked the commanders in charge, stripping Zongtang, Hongzhang, Henan governor Li Henian, and Zhili governor Guan Wen of their posts.

sentences.zh: 宗棠至保定，松山等連破賊深、祁、饒、晉。

translations.literal: When Zongtang reached Baoding, Songshan and others in succession defeated bandits at Shen, Qi, Rao, and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongtang reached Baoding, Songshan won a series of victories in Shen, Qi, Rao, and Jin.

sentences.zh: 當是時，捻馳騖數百里間，由直隸竄河南、山東，已復渡運越吳橋，犯天津。

translations.literal: At this time the Nian galloped over several hundred li, from Zhili fled into Henan and Shandong, had again crossed the Grand Canal beyond Wuqiao, and violated Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian ranged over hundreds of miles, broke from Zhili into Henan and Shandong, crossed the Grand Canal beyond Wuqiao, and threatened Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 鴻章議築長圍制賊；

translations.literal: Hongzhang proposed building a long encirclement to control the bandits;
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang proposed a long encirclement;

sentences.zh: 宗棠謂當且防且剿，西岸固守，必東路有追剿之師，乃可掣其狂奔之勢：上兩從其議。

translations.literal: Zongtang said one should both defend and pursue, hold firm on the west bank, and there must be pursuing troops on the east route before the momentum of their wild flight could be checked: the throne accepted both proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang argued for simultaneous defense and pursuit, holding the west bank while eastern columns chased the Nian down. The throne accepted both plans.

sentences.zh: 於是勤王師大集，宗棠駐軍吳橋，捻徘徊陵邑、濟陽，合淮、豫軍迭敗之，總愚走河濱以死，西捻平。

translations.literal: Thereupon armies rushing to aid the throne gathered in force; Zongtang encamped at Wuqiao; the Nian lingered at Lingyi and Jiyang; joining Huai and Yu armies they repeatedly defeated them; Zongyu fled to the riverbank and died; the western Nian were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Relief armies massed. Zongtang held Wuqiao while the Nian lingered near Lingyi and Jiyang. Combined Huai and Henan forces defeated them again and again until Zongyu died on the riverbank and the western Nian were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 入覲，天語褒嘉，且詢西陲師期。

translations.literal: On entering audience, the imperial words praised him, and moreover inquired the timetable for the western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At court audience the emperor praised him and asked how long the western campaign would take.

sentences.zh: 宗棠對以五年，後卒如其言焉。

translations.literal: Zongtang answered five years; later it indeed ended as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang answered five years, and in the end he was proved right.

sentences.zh: 七年十月，率師還陝，抵西安。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventh year, he led the army back to Shaanxi and reached Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of 1868 he led his army back to Shaanxi and reached Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 時東北土寇董福祥等眾十餘萬，擾延安、綏德，西南陝回白彥虎等號二十萬，踞甘肅董志原。

translations.literal: At that time in the northeast local bandits such as Dong Fuxiang numbered more than a hundred thousand and harassed Yan'an and Suide; in the southwest Shaanxi Muslims such as Bai Yanhu claimed two hundred thousand and held Dongzhiyuan in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the northeast local bandits led by Dong Fuxiang, more than a hundred thousand strong, harassed Yan'an and Suide, while in the southwest Shaanxi Muslim leader Bai Yanhu claimed two hundred thousand men and held Dongzhiyuan in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 松山至，破土寇，降福祥；

translations.literal: When Songshan arrived, he broke the local bandits and received Fuxiang's surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Songshan broke the local bandits and accepted Fuxiang's surrender;

sentences.zh: 而回益四出剿掠，其西南竄出者，並力擾秦川，黃鼎破之。

translations.literal: but Muslims increasingly raided on all sides; those who fled out southwest combined forces to harass the Qin plain; Huang Ding defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: but Muslim raids intensified on every side. Bands breaking southwest harassed the Qin plain until Huang Ding defeated them.

sentences.zh: 宗棠進軍乾州，諜報回巢將徙金積堡，分軍擊之，遂下董志原，連复鎮原、慶陽，回死者至三萬。

translations.literal: Zongtang advanced to Qianzhou; spies reported the Muslim nest would move to Jinjibu; he divided the army to strike, then took Dongzhiyuan, and in succession recovered Zhenyuan and Qingyang; Muslim dead reached thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang advanced to Qianzhou. Intelligence said the rebels would move to Jinjibu. He divided his force, took Dongzhiyuan, recovered Zhenyuan and Qingyang in succession, and killed thirty thousand Muslims.

sentences.zh: 督丁壯耕作，教以區田、代田法。

translations.literal: He supervised able-bodied men in farming and taught them the methods of zoned fields and rotation fields.
translations.idiomatic: He set the able-bodied to farming and taught them zoned-field and crop-rotation methods.

sentences.zh: 擇嶮荒地，發帑金巨萬，悉取所收饑民及降眾十七萬居焉。

translations.literal: He selected rugged wasteland, disbursed treasury funds in the tens of thousands, and settled there all the famine refugees and surrendered masses numbering one hundred seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He chose rugged wasteland, spent vast sums from the treasury, and settled there one hundred seventy thousand refugees and surrendered people.

sentences.zh: 遂以八年五月進駐涇州。

translations.literal: He then in the fifth month of the eighth year advanced and encamped at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of 1869 he advanced his headquarters to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 甘回最著者，西曰馬朵三，踞西寧；

translations.literal: The most prominent Gansu Muslims were: in the west Ma Duosan, holding Xining;
translations.idiomatic: The leading Gansu Muslim leaders were Ma Duosan in the west at Xining;

sentences.zh: 南曰馬占鰲，踞河川；

translations.literal: in the south Ma Zhan'ao, holding Hechuan;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhan'ao in the south at Hechuan;

sentences.zh: 北曰馬化隆，踞寧夏、靈州。

translations.literal: in the north Ma Hualong, holding Ningxia and Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and Ma Hualong in the north at Ningxia and Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 化隆以金積堡為老巢，堡當秦、漢兩渠間，扼黃河之險，擅鹽、馬、茶大利。

translations.literal: Hualong took Jinjibu as his old nest; the fort lay between the Qin and Han canals, commanding the Yellow River's strategic point, monopolizing great profits in salt, horses, and tea.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong made Jinjibu his stronghold. The fort lay between the Qin and Han canals, commanding the Yellow River crossing and monopolizing the salt, horse, and tea trades.

sentences.zh: 環堡五百餘寨，黨眾嘯聚。

translations.literal: More than five hundred stockades surrounded the fort, and party followers gathered with a shout.
translations.idiomatic: More than five hundred stockades ringed the fort, and his followers massed there.

sentences.zh: 掠取漢民產業子女。

translations.literal: They plundered Han civilians' property and children.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Han property and abducted Han women and children.

sentences.zh: 陝回時時與通市，相為首尾。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Muslims constantly traded with them, acting as head and tail to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Muslims traded with them constantly and acted in concert.

sentences.zh: 化隆以新教煽回民，購馬造軍械，而陽輸誠紿穆圖善。

translations.literal: Hualong used the New Teaching to stir Muslims, purchased horses and made weapons, yet openly professed loyalty to deceive Mutu Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong stirred the Muslims with the New Teaching, bought horses, and manufactured arms, while openly professing loyalty to deceive Mutu Shan.

sentences.zh: 董志原既平，陝回竄靈州，化隆上書為陝回乞撫。

translations.literal: After Dongzhiyuan was pacified, Shaanxi Muslims fled to Lingzhou; Hualong memorialized begging pacification for Shaanxi Muslims.
translations.idiomatic: After Dongzhiyuan fell, Shaanxi Muslims fled to Lingzhou and Hualong memorialized asking peace terms for them.

sentences.zh: 宗棠察其詐，備三月糧，先攻金積堡，以為收功全隴之基。

translations.literal: Zongtang perceived his deceit, prepared three months' provisions, and first attacked Jinjibu, taking this as the foundation for completing the pacification of all Long.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang saw through the ruse, laid in three months' provisions, and attacked Jinjibu first as the key to pacifying all Gansu.

sentences.zh: 及松山追陝回至靈州，扼永靈洞。

translations.literal: When Songshan pursued Shaanxi Muslims to Lingzhou, he seized Yongling Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Songshan pursued the Shaanxi Muslims to Lingzhou and seized Yongling Pass.

sentences.zh: 化隆懼，仍代陝回乞撫，謀緩兵，穆圖善信之，日言撫，綏遠城將軍至劾松山濫殺激變。

translations.literal: Hualong grew afraid and again begged pacification on behalf of Shaanxi Muslims, plotting to slow the army; Mutu Shan believed him and daily spoke of pacification; the Suiyuan garrison general arrived and impeached Songshan for indiscriminate killing that provoked rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong, alarmed, again pleaded for peace on behalf of the Shaanxi Muslims to gain time. Mutu Shan believed him and talked daily of negotiation. The Suiyuan garrison general impeached Songshan for indiscriminate killing that had provoked rebellion.

sentences.zh: 然化隆實無意降也，密召諸回並出劫軍餉。

translations.literal: Yet Hualong in fact had no intention of surrendering; he secretly summoned all Muslims to come out together and plunder army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: But Hualong had no intention of surrendering and secretly ordered all Muslim bands out to raid army supplies.

sentences.zh: 十一月，宗棠進駐平涼。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Zongtang advanced and encamped at Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zongtang moved his headquarters to Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 九年，松山陣歿，以其兄子錦棠代之，戰屢捷，而中路、南路軍亦所向有功，陝回受撫者數千人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Songshan fell in battle; his elder brother's son Jintang replaced him; battles were repeatedly victorious, and central-route and southern-route armies also achieved success wherever they went; Shaanxi Muslims who accepted pacification numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 Songshan was killed in battle and his nephew Jintang replaced him. Victory followed victory on the central and southern fronts, and several thousand Shaanxi Muslims submitted.

sentences.zh: 及奪秦壩關，化隆益窘，詣軍門乞降，誅之，夷其城堡。

translations.literal: When Qinba Pass was taken, Hualong grew ever more pressed; he came to the army gate begging surrender; he was executed and his fort and castle leveled.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinba Pass fell, Hualong was cornered. He came to the camp begging to surrender, was executed, and his fortifications were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 遷甘回固原、平涼，陝回化平，而編管鈐束之，寧、靈悉定。

translations.literal: Gansu Muslims were relocated to Guyuan and Pingliang; Shaanxi Muslims were settled at Huaping and placed under organized control and restraint; Ning and Ling were entirely settled.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu Muslims were resettled at Guyuan and Pingliang, Shaanxi Muslims at Huaping under strict control, and Ningxia and Lingzhou were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 奏言進規河湟，而是時有伊犁之變，詔宗棠分兵屯肅州，乃遣徐佔彪將六千人往。

translations.literal: He memorialized proposing to advance against the Huang and Huangshui region; but at this time the Yili affair arose; an edict ordered Zongtang to divide troops and garrison Suzhou; he then dispatched Xu Zhanbiao leading six thousand men thither.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to advance on the Huangshui region, but the Yili crisis intervened. The court ordered troops garrisoned at Suzhou, and he sent Xu Zhanbiao west with six thousand men.

sentences.zh: 十年七月，自率大軍由平涼移駐靜寧。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the tenth year, he personally led the great army from Pingliang to encamp at Jingning.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 1871 he led the main army from Pingliang to Jingning.

sentences.zh: 八月，至安定。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, he reached Anding.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he reached Anding.

sentences.zh: 寇聚河州，其東出，必繞洮河三甲集，集西太子寺，再西大東鄉，皆險要。

translations.literal: Bandits gathered at Hezhou; if they came out east they must circle the Tao River's Sanjiaji, west of the ji was Taizi Temple, and further west Dadongxiang—all strategically vital.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels massed at Hezhou. Any eastern breakout had to pass Sanjiaji on the Tao River, then Taizi Temple, then Dadongxiang—all formidable positions.

sentences.zh: 諸將分擊，悉破平之。

translations.literal: The generals attacked separately and all were defeated and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: His generals attacked on separate fronts and cleared them all.

sentences.zh: 時回酋朵三已死，佔鰲見官軍深入，西寧回已歸順，去路絕，遂亦受撫。

translations.literal: At that time Muslim chief Duosan was already dead; Zhan'ao, seeing government troops penetrate deeply and Xining Muslims already submitted, with escape routes cut off, then also accepted pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Duosan was already dead. Zhan'ao, seeing the army deep in his territory, Xining Muslims already submitted, and escape cut off, also accepted pacification.

sentences.zh: 河州平。

translations.literal: Hezhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 十一年七月，移駐蘭州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eleventh year, he moved his headquarters to Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 1872 he moved his headquarters to Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 佔彪前以伊犁之變率師而西也，於時肅州阻亂，回酋馬文祿先已就撫，聞關外兵事急，复據城叛。

translations.literal: Zhanbiao had earlier because of the Yili affair led his army west; at that time Suzhou was obstructed by disorder; Muslim chief Ma Wenlu had first already submitted, but hearing frontier military affairs were urgent, again seized the city and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanbiao had earlier marched west because of the Yili crisis. At Suzhou, Muslim leader Ma Wenlu had once submitted, but hearing of troubles beyond the passes he rebelled and seized the city again.

sentences.zh: 及佔彪軍至，乃嬰城固守，而乞援西寧。

translations.literal: When Zhanbiao's army arrived, he then clung to the city in stubborn defense and begged aid from Xining.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhanbiao's army arrived, he shut himself in the city and begged Xining for help.

sentences.zh: 陝回白彥虎、禹得彥亦潛應文祿。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Muslims Bai Yanhu and Yu Deyan also secretly responded to Wenlu.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Muslim leaders Bai Yanhu and Yu Deyan also secretly supported Wenlu.

sentences.zh: 會錦棠率軍至，西寧土回及陝回俱變，推馬本源為元帥。

translations.literal: It happened that Jintang led his army there; Xining native Muslims and Shaanxi Muslims all rebelled and made Ma Benyuan commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Jintang arrived, Xining's native and Shaanxi Muslims both rose and made Ma Benyuan their commander.

sentences.zh: 西寧東北阻湟水，兩山對峙，古所稱湟中也。

translations.literal: Northeast of Xining the Huang River blocks the way; two mountains face each other—the region anciently called Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast of Xining the Huang River blocks the way between facing mountains—the region anciently called Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 賊據險而屯，俄敗走，遺棄馬騾滿山谷，竄巴燕戎格。

translations.literal: Bandits held the strategic points and encamped; soon they were defeated and fled, abandoning horses and mules that filled the valleys, fleeing to Bayan Rongge.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the heights but were soon routed, leaving horses and mules strewn through the valleys as they fled to Bayan Rongge.

sentences.zh: 大通都司馬壽复嗾向陽堡回殺漢民以叛。

translations.literal: Datong company commander Ma Shou again incited Xiangyang Fort Muslims to kill Han civilians and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Datong company commander Ma Shou again incited the Muslims of Xiangyang Fort to massacre Han civilians and rebel.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，錦棠攻向陽堡，奪門入，斬馬壽，遂破大通，搗巴燕戎格，誅本源，河東、西諸回堡皆降。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year, Jintang attacked Xiangyang Fort, seized the gate and entered, beheaded Ma Shou, then broke Datong, struck Bayan Rongge, executed Benyuan; all Muslim forts east and west of the river submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1873 Jintang stormed Xiangyang Fort, cut down Ma Shou, broke Datong, struck Bayan Rongge, executed Benyuan, and all Muslim forts east and west of the river submitted.

sentences.zh: 文祿踞肅州，詭詞求撫，益招致邊外回助城守，連攻未能下。

translations.literal: Wenlu held Suzhou, using deceitful words to beg pacification, further recruiting frontier Muslims to aid in defending the city; repeated attacks could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenlu held Suzhou, pleading for peace in deceit while recruiting frontier Muslims to defend the city. Repeated assaults failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 八月，宗棠來視師，文祿登城見帥旗，奪氣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Zongtang came to inspect the army; Wenlu ascended the wall, saw the commander's banner, and lost his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zongtang came to direct the siege. Wenlu saw the commander's banner from the wall and lost heart.

sentences.zh: 請出關討賊自效，不許。

translations.literal: He requested to go beyond the passes to attack bandits and prove his merit; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He offered to campaign beyond the passes to prove his loyalty, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 金順、錦棠軍大集，文祿窮蹙出降，磔之。

translations.literal: Jin Shun's and Jintang's armies gathered in force; Wenlu, pressed to extremity, came out and surrendered and was dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: With the armies of Jin Shun and Jintang massed, Wenlu surrendered in desperation and was executed by dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 白彥虎竄遁關外，肅州平。

translations.literal: Bai Yanhu fled in disorder beyond the passes; Suzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yanhu fled beyond the passes, and Suzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 以陝甘總督協辦大學士，加一等輕車都尉。

translations.literal: As Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general and assisting Grand Secretary, he was given the first-class title of Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: As governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu and assisting Grand Secretary, he was raised to first-class Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 奏請甘肅分闈鄉試，設學政。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting separate provincial examination gates for Gansu and the establishment of an educational commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for a separate provincial examination circuit in Gansu and the appointment of an educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十三年，晉東閣大學士，留治所。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and remained at his governing post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1874 he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion while remaining at his post.

sentences.zh: 自咸豐初，天下大亂，粵盜最劇，次者捻逆，次者回。

translations.literal: From the beginning of Xianfeng, the empire fell into great disorder: Guangdong bandits were most severe, next the Nian rebels, next the Muslims.
translations.idiomatic: Since the early Xianfeng years the empire had been torn by rebellion: the Taiping were worst, then the Nian, then the Muslim uprisings.

sentences.zh: 宗棠既手戡定之，至是陝、甘悉靖，而塞外平回，朝廷尤矜寵焉。

translations.literal: Zongtang had personally suppressed and settled them; by this time Shaanxi and Gansu were entirely pacified, and beyond the passes the Muslims were pacified; the court especially cherished and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang had personally suppressed all three. Shaanxi and Gansu were now quiet, and the frontier Muslims were pacified as well. The court showered him with favor.

sentences.zh: 塞外回酋曰帕夏，本安集延部之和碩伯克也。

translations.literal: The frontier Muslim chief called Pasha was originally a Heshuo beik of the Kokand department.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier Muslim leader known as the Pasha was originally a Kokand noble of Heshuo rank.

sentences.zh: 安集延故屬敖罕，敖罕為俄羅斯所滅，安集延獨存。

translations.literal: Kokand formerly belonged to Kokand Khanate; Kokand Khanate was destroyed by Russia, and Kokand alone survived.
translations.idiomatic: Kokand had once belonged to the Khanate of Kokand, which Russia destroyed, leaving Kokand itself standing.

sentences.zh: 帕夏畏俄逼，闌入邊。

translations.literal: The Pasha, fearing Russian pressure, forced his way across the border.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Russian pressure, the Pasha forced his way across the border.

sentences.zh: 據喀什噶爾，稍蠶食南八城，又攻敗烏魯木齊所踞回妥明。

translations.literal: He seized Kashgar, gradually nibbled away the southern eight cities, and again attacked and defeated the Muslim Tuoming who held Urumqi.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Kashgar, gradually swallowed the southern eight cities, and defeated Tuoming, the Muslim leader holding Urumqi.

sentences.zh: 妥明者，西寧回也，初以新教遊關外。

translations.literal: Tuoming was a Xining Muslim who at first traveled beyond the passes preaching the New Teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoming was a Xining Muslim who had first wandered beyond the passes preaching the New Teaching.

sentences.zh: 同治初，乘陝甘漢、回構變倡亂，據烏城。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi, taking advantage of Han-Muslim strife in Shaanxi and Gansu, he raised rebellion and held Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign he exploited Han-Muslim conflict in Shaanxi and Gansu to raise rebellion and seize Urumqi.

sentences.zh: 帕夏既攻敗妥明降之，遂並有北路伊犁諸城，收其賦入。

translations.literal: After the Pasha attacked, defeated, and received Tuoming's surrender, he then also possessed the northern-route cities of Yili and collected their tax revenues.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Tuoming and accepting his surrender, the Pasha also took the northern cities of Yili and collected their revenues.

sentences.zh: 妥明旋被逐，走死，而白彥虎竄處烏城，仍隸帕夏。

translations.literal: Tuoming was soon driven out and fled to his death; Bai Yanhu fled to Wucheng and still submitted to the Pasha.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoming was soon driven out and died in flight. Bai Yanhu remained at Urumqi under the Pasha's command.

sentences.zh: 帕夏能屬役回眾，通使結援英、俄，購兵械自備。

translations.literal: The Pasha could employ Muslim masses, send envoys to ally with Britain and Russia, and purchase weapons to equip himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Pasha could command the Muslim population, send envoys to Britain and Russia, and buy arms for his forces.

sentences.zh: 英人陰助之，欲令別立為國，用捍蔽俄。

translations.literal: The English secretly aided him, wishing to have him established as a separate state to shield against Russia.
translations.idiomatic: The British secretly supported him, hoping to set up a separate state as a buffer against Russia.

sentences.zh: 當是時，俄以回數擾其邊境，遽引兵逐回，取伊犁，且言將代取烏魯木齊。

translations.literal: At that time Russia, because Muslims repeatedly harassed its borders, suddenly led troops to drive out the Muslims, took Yili, and moreover said it would take Urumqi on China's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Russia, citing Muslim raids on its border, suddenly marched in, drove out the rebels, seized Yili, and offered to take Urumqi on China's behalf.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，宗棠既平關隴，將出關，而海防議起。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu, after Zongtang had pacified Guan and Long and was about to go beyond the passes, debate over coastal defense arose.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875, after Zongtang had pacified Shaanxi and Gansu and was preparing to march west, debate erupted over coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 論者多言自高宗定新疆，歲糜數百萬，此漏卮也。

translations.literal: Discussants mostly said that since the Gaozong Emperor settled Xinjiang, millions were wasted yearly—this was a leaking vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that since the Qianlong Emperor had conquered Xinjiang, millions had been wasted there every year—a bottomless drain.

sentences.zh: 今至竭天下力贍西軍，無以待不虞，尤失計。

translations.literal: Now to exhaust the empire's strength supplying the western army, leaving nothing for unforeseen events, was especially a mistaken plan.
translations.idiomatic: To exhaust the empire's resources on the western army and leave nothing for emergencies was especially misguided.

sentences.zh: 宜徇英人議，許帕夏自立為國稱籓，罷西征，專力海防。

translations.literal: One should follow the English proposal, permit the Pasha to establish himself as a state and pay tribute, halt the western expedition, and concentrate on coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: They urged following the British proposal: let the Pasha rule as a tributary state, halt the western expedition, and concentrate on coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 鴻章言之尤力。

translations.literal: Hongzhang spoke on this with especial force.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang argued this most forcefully.

sentences.zh: 宗棠曰：「關隴新平，不及時規還國家舊所沒地，而割棄使別為國，此坐自遺患。

translations.literal: Zongtang said: "Guan and Long are newly pacified; if we do not in time plan to recover the territory the state formerly lost, but instead cede and abandon it so it becomes a separate state, this is to sit and bequeath calamity upon ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang replied: "With Shaanxi and Gansu just pacified, to abandon recovered territory and let it become a separate state is to invite disaster.

sentences.zh: 萬一帕夏不能有，不西為英並，即北折而入俄耳。

translations.literal: In the event the Pasha cannot hold it, he will not be annexed westward by Britain but will turn north and enter Russia.
translations.idiomatic: If the Pasha cannot hold it, Britain will not take it from the west; Russia will seize it from the north.

sentences.zh: 吾地坐縮，邊要盡失，防邊兵不可減，糜餉自若。

translations.literal: Our territory will simply shrink, frontier strongpoints all be lost, frontier-defense troops cannot be reduced, and wasted provisions continue as before.
translations.idiomatic: Our territory will shrink, frontier defenses will collapse, border garrisons cannot be reduced, and spending will continue unchecked.

sentences.zh: 無益海防而挫國威，且長亂。

translations.literal: It will not benefit coastal defense but will damage national prestige and moreover prolong disorder.
translations.idiomatic: It will not help coastal defense, will damage national prestige, and will prolong disorder.

sentences.zh: 此必不可。」

translations.literal: This absolutely cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: This must not be done."

sentences.zh: 軍機大臣文祥獨善宗棠議，遂決策出塞，不罷兵。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Wen Xiang alone approved Zongtang's proposal; the decision was then made to go beyond the passes and not halt the army.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Wen Xiang alone sided with Zongtang, and the court decided to march beyond the passes without halting the army.

sentences.zh: 授宗棠欽差大臣，督軍事，金順副之。

translations.literal: Zongtang was appointed Imperial Commissioner to supervise military affairs, with Jin Shun as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang was appointed Imperial Commissioner to direct military affairs, with Jin Shun as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，次肅州。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, he halted at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1876 he halted at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，錦棠北逾天山，會金順軍先攻烏魯木齊，克之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Jintang crossed the Tianshan northward, joined Jin Shun's army in first attacking Urumqi, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Jintang crossed the Tianshan northward, joined Jin Shun, and took Urumqi.

sentences.zh: 白彥虎遁走托克遜。

translations.literal: Bai Yanhu fled in disorder to Toksun.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yanhu fled to Toksun.

sentences.zh: 九月，克瑪納斯南城，北路平，乃規南路。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the southern city of Manas was captured; the northern route was pacified, and then the southern route was planned.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the southern city of Manas fell, the northern route was pacified, and planning turned to the south.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「回部為安酋驅迫，厭亂久矣。

translations.literal: An order said: "The Muslim regions have long been driven and compelled by the Kokand chief and are weary of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: "The Muslim peoples have long been driven by the Kokand ruler and are weary of war.

sentences.zh: 大軍所至，勿淫掠，勿殘殺。

translations.literal: Where the great army arrives, do not plunder licentiously, do not slaughter wantonly.
translations.idiomatic: Where the army goes, do not plunder or slaughter wantonly.

sentences.zh: 王者之師如時雨，此其時也。」

translations.literal: The army of a true king is like timely rain—this is the time for it."
translations.idiomatic: The army of a true king is like timely rain. Now is the time."

sentences.zh: 三年三月，錦棠攻克達坂城，悉釋所擒纏回，縱之歸。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year, Jintang captured Dabancheng, released all captured Turfan Muslims, and let them return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1877 Jintang took Dabancheng, released all captured Turfan Muslims, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 南路恟懼，翼日，收托克遜城，而佔彪及孫金彪兩軍亦連破諸城隘，合羅長祜等軍收吐魯番，降纏回萬餘。

translations.literal: The southern route was shaken with fear; the next day Toksun city was taken; meanwhile Zhanbiao's and Sun Jinbiao's two armies also in succession broke various city passes; joining Luo Changhu's army they recovered Turfan; more than ten thousand Turfan Muslims submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The southern route panicked. The next day Toksun fell. Zhanbiao and Sun Jinbiao broke pass after pass, joined Luo Changhu, recovered Turfan, and more than ten thousand Muslims submitted.

sentences.zh: 帕夏飲藥死，其子伯克胡里戕其弟，走喀什噶爾。
